title: Heart failure, new and changed medicines, Spanish
source:
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS - Riverside General Hospital, Cardiology Unit
Patient: Maria Lopez   MRN: 00482913   DOB: 03/14/1953
Attending: Dr. Anil Patel
Discharge date: 10/14/2026

Principal diagnosis: Acute decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 30%), precipitated by dietary sodium indiscretion and NSAID use.

Hospital course: Patient admitted with dyspnea, orthopnea and bilateral lower-extremity edema. Diuresed with IV furosemide, net negative 4.2 L. Creatinine rose transiently to 1.6 mg/dL and improved to 1.3 mg/dL at discharge.

MEDICATIONS
NEW: Spironolactone 25 mg by mouth once daily
CHANGED: Furosemide increased from 20 mg to 40 mg by mouth twice daily (8 AM and 2 PM)
HOLD: Ibuprofen - do not take until kidney function is rechecked by your cardiologist
STOP: Lisinopril 10 mg daily - discontinued
NEW: Sacubitril/valsartan 24/26 mg by mouth twice daily. Do not take within 36 hours of your last lisinopril dose.
CONTINUE: Metoprolol succinate 50 mg by mouth once daily

Return precautions: Return to the Emergency Department or call 911 for chest pain, shortness of breath at rest, or fainting. Call the heart failure clinic at (555) 201-3344 if weight increases by more than 2 lb in one day or 5 lb in one week, or if leg swelling worsens.

Diet: Sodium restriction < 2 g/day. Fluid restriction 1.5 L/day.
Activity: Weigh yourself every morning after urinating and before breakfast and record daily weights. Walk as tolerated; no lifting > 10 lb for 2 weeks.

Follow-up: Heart failure clinic with Dr. Patel on 10/21/2026 at 10:30 AM. Basic metabolic panel (blood test) on 10/18/2026 at the outpatient lab.
